explainer_content.short_definition: The 1980s US punk pressure cooker: faster, cheaper, louder, and more self-organized.
explainer_content.history_capsule: Hardcore took punk's permission structure and rebuilt it through regional scenes, indie labels, vans, basement shows, and all-ages rooms.
explainer_content.why_it_mattered: It created the underground logistics that later alternative, emo, post-hardcore, and indie scenes inherited.
explainer_content.what_made_it_distinct: Speed, barked vocals, tight riffs, and anti-commercial infrastructure distinguish it from both first-wave punk and metal.
